nodes.title: PersonSignedUp
nodes.description:
Someone creates an account. They start `UNVOUCHED`: they can read and write, but their claims and publications only show to themselves and moderators until someone vouches for them.

Rate limits per account apply from the start, whatever the standing.

nodes.title: PersonVouched
nodes.description:
A vouched person vouches for someone else, with a reason in their own words ("we did a mutirão together in 2024", "video call on 3 November"). Only someone `VOUCHED` at that moment can vouch, so trust only spreads from people who already have it.

A moderator approving a newcomer is a vouch like any other, so there's one mechanism instead of two. The vouch is public: the vouched person's profile lists who vouched for them.
nodes.openQuestions:
- How many vouches does it take? One is enough for a small community where moderators can revoke.
- Can a voucher withdraw their own vouch (a `VouchWithdrawn` event)?
- Should a person be limited to a number of vouches per month, so one compromised account can't bring in a crowd?

nodes.title: PersonReported
nodes.description:
Someone reports a profile itself, not a piece of its content:
- `AUTOMATED`: a bot or a language model posing as a person.
- `IMPERSONATION`: pretending to be another person or organization.
- `SPAM` and `ABUSIVE`: a pattern across the profile, beyond a single claim (single claims use ClaimReported).

Unlike conduct reports on a claim, an open profile report hides nothing, because hiding everything a person wrote on one report invites pile-ons. It only reaches the moderation queue.
nodes.exampleSchema:
Schema.Struct({
  reportId: Schema.NonEmptyString.pipe(Schema.brand("PersonReportId")),
  personId: PersonId,
  reason: Schema.Literals(["AUTOMATED", "IMPERSONATION", "SPAM", "ABUSIVE"]),
  note: Schema.optionalKey(Schema.NonEmptyString),
  reporterId: PersonId,
  reportedAt: Schema.DateTimeUtcFromString,
})

nodes.title: PersonStandingDecided
nodes.description:
A moderator decides on a person's standing:
- `BLOCK`: everything they wrote is hidden from everyone but them and moderators, and they can't vouch or report.
- `UNBLOCK`: back to the standing their vouches give them.
- `REVOKE_VOUCHES`: back to `UNVOUCHED`, for someone who isn't abusive but shouldn't have been brought in.
- `KEEP`: settle the reports without changing anything.

It can settle open profile reports, but doesn't need one: a block can also come from the queue's repeated-conduct item. Blocking is never automatic.
nodes.exampleSchema:
Schema.Struct({
  personId: PersonId,
  decision: Schema.Literals(["BLOCK", "UNBLOCK", "REVOKE_VOUCHES", "KEEP"]),
  settlesReportIds: Schema.Array(Schema.NonEmptyString.pipe(Schema.brand("PersonReportId"))),
  reason: Schema.NonEmptyString,
  decidedByPersonId: PersonId,
  decidedAt: Schema.DateTimeUtcFromString,
})
nodes.openQuestions: - The app's `canModifyAccessLevel` refuses moving anyone back to `NEWCOMER`. `REVOKE_VOUCHES` needs that rule to go, or `UNVOUCHED` to be separate from `NEWCOMER`.

nodes.title: ClaimReported
nodes.description: From the article projections canvas: someone reports a claim or an external value. Shown here because reports from blocked people are ignored and reports from unvouched people rank lower.

nodes.title: ClaimReportSettled
nodes.description: From the article projections canvas: a moderator's verdict on a target's open reports. Upheld conduct verdicts count against the claim's authors, and through them, against their vouchers.

nodes.title: ResolvePersonStanding
nodes.description:
Derive each person's standing from the events, never stored as a column:
1. `BLOCKED` if their latest standing decision is `BLOCK`.
2. Otherwise `VOUCHED` if they have a vouch from someone who was `VOUCHED` when vouching, made after their latest `REVOKE_VOUCHES`.
3. Otherwise `UNVOUCHED`.

Because it's derived, every decision is reversible: unblocking or vouching again brings the person's past claims back. Blocking a voucher doesn't unvouch the people they vouched for: the moderation queue lists them for review instead.

Also indexes vouches by voucher, and keeps open profile reports for the queue.
nodes.openQuestions: - Should blocking a voucher hide their vouchees' claims until someone reviews them, instead of only listing them?

nodes.title: ResolveClaimVisibility
nodes.description:
From the article projections canvas, with one change: it reads StandingByPersonId to ignore reports from `BLOCKED` people and rank reports from `UNVOUCHED` people lower.

ClaimVisibilityById stays sparse and keyed by reported target. It doesn't get an entry for every claim of an unvouched person: readers combine it with the author's standing.

nodes.title: StandingByPersonId
nodes.description: Each person's standing, with the vouches that give it (who and why) or the decision that blocked them. People without an entry are `UNVOUCHED`.

nodes.title: VouchesByVoucherId
nodes.description: Who each person vouched for, and when. Used to hold vouchers accountable and to review a blocked voucher's vouchees.

nodes.title: OpenPersonReportsByPersonId
nodes.description: Profile reports without a standing decision, per reported person, with every report's reason and reporter.

nodes.title: ClaimVisibilityById
nodes.description: From the article projections canvas: visibility of every reported target. Targets without an entry are visible, unless their author's standing says otherwise.

nodes.title: ReportOutcomesByPersonId
nodes.description: From the article projections canvas: per person, upheld conduct verdicts on their claims and how their own reports were settled.

nodes.title: FilterVisibleClaims
nodes.description:
The one rule every article transformation applies before using a claim (ConsolidateArticleNames, SummarizeArticleHeights, SelectGbifTaxonId…). A claim from a `CONTRIBUTOR` or `INFERENCE` provenance is visible to a reader when:
- its author is `VOUCHED`, or the reader is the author or a moderator, and
- ClaimVisibilityById doesn't hide it.

`EXTERNAL_PROVIDER` claims have no author and skip the standing check. Hidden claims also stay out of summaries, counts and selections.
nodes.openQuestions: - Should a canonical selection (a GBIF or Wikidata ID) ever come from an unvouched person's pending claim, seen only by them?

nodes.title: SummarizeVoucherRecords
nodes.description: For each voucher, count what happened to the people they vouched for: blocked, vouches revoked, or with upheld conduct verdicts. A voucher whose vouchees keep getting censored moves up the moderation queue. It's a nudge for a moderator to talk to them, not an automatic penalty.

nodes.title: ArticleDocument
nodes.description: From the article projections canvas: what readers see, already filtered by FilterVisibleClaims.

nodes.title: VoucherRecordsByPersonId
nodes.description: Per voucher: how many people they vouched for, and which of them were blocked, revoked or had upheld conduct verdicts.

nodes.title: BuildModerationQueue
nodes.description:
The person-related items it adds to the queue from the article projections canvas:
- People with open profile reports, `AUTOMATED` and `IMPERSONATION` first.
- People with repeated upheld conduct verdicts, for a blocking decision.
- People vouched for by someone who was just blocked, for review.
- Vouchers whose vouchees keep getting blocked or censored.

Newcomers no longer queue for a moderator's approval: they wait for anyone vouched to vouch for them.
nodes.openQuestions: - Should unvouched people who keep writing for weeks without a vouch show up somewhere, so a moderator can reach out?

nodes.title: ModerationQueue
nodes.description: From the article projections canvas: items awaiting a moderator, oldest first.
